original_card.question: Can a completed call earn more independent productive target credit without an offsetting paid bill?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Use #5599 as a completed positive control, then choose one uncovered cut/module beyond an applicable frozen exclusion. Derive independence, saturation and chronological availability rather than counting rational rank alone. Price target credits and all new jobs together, then check compiler and actual caller compatibility. Stop on a nonphysical credit or an unfavorable complete relaxation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Exact classification of the plane-level (source mask, reader mask) signatures that an invertible 4x4 matrix over any field can have, in the two-plane, four-message model of PR3997. Lemma 1 shows the signature depends only on two complementary 2-planes of K^4 (the row spaces of the top and bottom port pairs): sources test containment of a plane in a coordinate hyperplane, readers test containment of a coordinate vector in the other plane. Three necessary conditions follow; exactly 439 of 6,561 candidate signatures satisfy them, all 439 are realized by explicit integer matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}, and the set equals the 439 signature codes recorded by PR3997. Consequently special rational values add no signature, and PR3997's recorded minimum copy invoice 8 on each of 1,540 plane pairs holds for every invertible basis. That invoice consequence is not new: it agrees with the stronger rank theorem of PR4365 (research/two-plane-copy-floor), which proves COPY mass 8 for arbitrary scalar factorizations over every field. Corroborated by exhaustive plane-pair enumeration over F_2, F_3, F_5 (and F_7 opt-in) against direct matrix inversion, and a direct census of GL_4(F_2). No pricing is recomputed; no kappa changes.
scope_change_reason: The current card asks about independent productive target credit under a completed call. This package instead answers the open question left by PR3997 (research/rational-joint-support-screen, an earlier revision of this card): whether exact cofactor cancellations can add a plane-level signature that lowers its two-plane copy invoice. A later merged package, PR4365, settles the invoice-level gap by a rank proof; this package settles the signature-level question (which plane-level signatures an invertible basis can have) and does not claim the invoice floor as new. It is a side result on a decoder screen. It builds no supplier and changes no paid profile.
bottleneck_link: Side result. It removes coefficient cancellations as a way around PR3997's minimum copy invoice 8 for a joint 4x4 basis on two planes. It does not change any paid profile, supplier, invoice or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop when the realizable signature set is determined exactly by necessary conditions matched with explicit witnesses, or when a signature outside the generic 439 appears. Do not extend this package to three or more planes, overcomplete factorizations or coefficient pricing.
evidence: verify.py recomputes RESULT.json and WITNESSES.json: 6,561 candidate signatures, 439 pass C1-C3 (555/805/1,771 without C1/C2/C3), equal to the 439 codes in PR3997's TERNARY-SCREEN.txt (bound by SHA256), 439 integer witnesses verified by exact rational inversion, 362 ternary planes whose complementary pairs realize only elements of N, every complementary plane pair over F_2 (560), F_3 (10,530) and F_5 (503,750) priced by the plane rule and compared with direct inversion (all pairs at F_2 and F_3, every 61st at F_5), a direct census of all 20,160 matrices of GL_4(F_2), and 11 rejection controls. PROOF.md gives the written proof of Lemmas 1 and 2.

open_questions.question: Is the realizable plane-level signature set still the generic census for two planes of three ports (6x6 bases)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lemma 1 holds verbatim for two planes of d ports. If cancellation adds signatures at d = 3, the d = 2 closure here is special to small blocks and PR3997's baseline could be beaten at larger plane size.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate complementary ordered pairs of 3-planes in F_2^6 (1,395 planes, 714,240 pairs) by incidence data, compare with the necessary-condition set for 6x6, and check against a generic structural-matching census.
open_questions.blocked_by: The generic 6x6 census ranges over 2^36 supports and needs an incidence-based generator; the candidate set has 9^6 signatures.

open_questions.question: Do three planes of two ports each admit a signature outside the generic census?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR3997 lists mixing three or more planes as outside its scope, and PR4365's first open question asks for a genuinely joint three-plane decoder with 49 closure-pair tariffs, which appear to be the 7 x 7 source/reader masks of three planes. The reader test generalizes to 'e_j is not in the sum of the other planes', so a third plane is the next place a joint basis could change a signature.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate complementary plane triples in F_2^6 and F_3^6 by incidence data and compare their signatures with the generic 6x6 census restricted to three planes.
open_questions.blocked_by: 49^6 candidate signatures need symmetry reduction; no pricing of three-plane groups is recorded.

open_questions.question: Which pairs (support of P, support of P^-1) occur for 4x4 invertible matrices, that is, what are the cofactor zero-pattern strata the original question asked about?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only a pricing model that reads port-level supports would see these strata; the plane-level pricing of PR3997 does not.
open_questions.first_step: Classify the support pairs over F_3 by exhaustive enumeration of plane pairs with fixed bases, then lift to Q with witnesses.
open_questions.blocked_by: Support pairs depend on the chosen basis of each plane, so the classification quantifies over GL_2 x GL_2; no port-level pricing model has been written down.
